summary: Australia's cheapest new electric car, the Dolphin pairs a soft, comfortable ride with a surprisingly well-equipped, upscale-feeling cabin for the price, according to CarExpert, CarsGuide and WhichCar. Reviewers agree it is happiest as a city runabout: refined and efficient around town, but wind noise, mixed rear visibility and (on the base Essential) modest power blunt its appeal on the open road. It is not a driver's car, but on value and everyday livability it comfortably outpoints most petrol light hatches at a similar price.
pros: Lowest entry price of any new EV in Australia
Comfortable, well-controlled ride for the segment
Roomy cabin and quality-feeling trim materials for the price
Strong standard equipment including a large rotating touchscreen
Five-star ANCAP safety rating with comprehensive driver assist tech
cons: Underpowered Essential struggles with highway overtaking
Slow 7kW AC home charging versus rivals' 11kW
Small boot and restricted rear visibility
Steeper resale depreciation risk as BYD repeatedly cuts new prices
